profile.headline: Sr. Staff Embedded Software Engineer | BSW · Low-Power · Mech + Embedded Systems
profile.summary:
Embedded software engineer with a dual B.S.E. in Mechanical Engineering and Computer Systems Engineering (Arizona State), an M.S. in Computer Engineering, and 13 years across defense, aerospace, and automotive. From real-time IW/SATCOM SDR waveforms and DO-178C avionics to vehicle connectivity and AV telematics. Now owning multi-SoC BSW bring-up and factory EOL for telematics hardware (Qualcomm SA525 / Infineon TC387 / TI BLE), including coordinated low-power paths at ~100 µA shutdown and ~7 mA standby/S2R, after owning 4G/5G stacks from modem to cloud at always-on, tens-of-mA budgets.

I still use the mechanical foundation every day: schematic and power-rail partnership with hardware, bench metering across SW/HW boundaries, and side projects that touch actuation—including a 3D-printed SO-ARM101 for teleoperation and policy training. Earlier work includes vision-driven road detection with Arduino servo steering and an ARDrone path-following stack with ROS.

Previously at GM: led 10+ engineers on Connectivity Hub Module (cellular/Wi-Fi/BT), OnStar Gen12 telematics, eCall/NG eCall, and multi-modem stacks for Cruise AVs. Co-inventor, U.S. Patent App. 19/547,483 — Method and System to Reduce Packet Latency for Wireless Communications with Vehicles. Six Sigma Black Belt. Based in Phoenix; open to remote, San Diego, and Seattle.

positions.title: Sr. Staff Embedded Software Engineer
positions.locationName: Mountain View, California, United States · Remote
positions.description:
• Own BSW bring-up and factory EOL for an automotive telematics module across Qualcomm SA525 (Yocto Linux), Infineon TC387 (FreeRTOS), and TI BLE (FreeRTOS), including multi-chip flash for 1K+ units.
• Implement coordinated power sequencing (MCU/BLE BSW + NAD path via Qualcomm S2R APIs) to ~100 µA shutdown and ~7 mA standby/S2R at 12 V for vehicle-level soak without draining the battery; verify with INA219/INA228 and RPi-based power metering.
• Deliver flashable binary images for factory EOL and pre-factory validation; BSW exercises GNSS, cellular modem, low-power current gates, and wake paths over CAN and BLE GATT.
• Run an AI-assisted closed-loop bench (Codex + Jira/repos, SSH to remote fixtures, Azure pipeline flash) for on-target iterate-and-measure; publish reusable context/skills the team uses for Jira, lab loop, package delivery, and proposal review. Partner with HW to map schematic/power-rail intent into SW under test.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Wrote middleware software interfacing with Qualcomm SA525 5G Modem APIs to establish cellular data connectivity for the vehicle, designed as an always-on data connection in low power modes. Supported cloud transport protocols for remote commands and emergency notifications.

• Team lead of 10+ senior and junior software engineers developing Connectivity Hub Module (CHM) Cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth capabilities and integration with the Infotainment ECU.

• Co-inventor on U.S. Patent Application No. 19/547,483 — Method and System to Reduce Packet Latency for Wireless Communications with Vehicles (recorded February 2026).

• Developed eCall and Next Generation eCall (NG eCall) emergency calling systems over IMS/LTE, implementing 3GPP-defined (TS 26.267/TS 26.268) life-safety voice and data channels with priority bearer handling to ensure emergency services connectivity during vehicle incidents.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Wrote middleware software that established 4G/5G cellular network connectivity for the OnStar Telematics Module (Gen12) and supported emergency calls with extensive connection retry logic for establishing an OnStar advisor connection.

• Developed software stack for the Multi Carrier Telematics Module (MCTM) on Cruise Autonomous Vehicles, splitting data packets across 3 Qualcomm SA415M 4G modems and re-ordering them on the backend of IPSec tunnels, achieving ~45 MB theoretical upload throughput.

• Implemented a GStreamer pipeline with RTP transport and ALSA audio integration for the MCTM, enabling real-time media streaming from the autonomous vehicle to the backend operations center.

• Built a local web server to support vehicle controls for riders in-vehicle via an Android app UI.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Next Generation Communications Software Design and Development

- Autonomous Vehicle Communications Software Design and Development

positions.title: Engineer II Software
positions.description:
Embedded application design, development, and testing to log data from HTF ECUs in C#.

Engineering software development of HTF ECU for test development in C++.

Product-line configuration management plan implementation for systems and software per ARP4754A, DO-178C, and DO-331.

Product-line systems and software requirements implementation in DOORS.

positions.title: Embedded Software Engineer II
positions.description: Software/Hardware Integration

positions.title: Software Engineer I
positions.description:
Software development on BOWMAN ComBAT system.

Software maintenance on HMS platform.

Software design and implementation of the Integrated Waveform (IW) on the Digital Modular Radio (DMR).
• Implemented multi-thread algorithms on VxWorks for real-time communication of IW.
• Development of network acquisition firmware to interface with an FPGA for signal processing.
• Developed overnight Software/Firmware testbench for energy detection testing.
• Wrote approximately 10K+ SLOC and reviewed 50K+ SLOC.

company.name: Cyber-Phsical Systems Lab at Arizona State University

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description:
Implemented Software-In-Loop and Processor-In-Loop tests with MatLab/SimuLink for a Engine Control Unit (ECU) Model on a single core Renesas V850 board with both CAN bus and serial port protocols.

Researched for the development of parallelizable code with MatLab/Simulink Embedded Coder of the ECU model for a dual-core processor.

Researched for the development of a real-time scheduler for both the single and dual-core implementation of the ECU.

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description:
Conducted finite-element stress analysis of coil winding and identified structurally 
sound wire material and gauge for the Fault Current Limiter (FCL). 

Designed and machined a plastic modular magnet housing using SolidWorks.

Implemented firmware on TI DSP microcontroller to control a low voltage model of the FCL.

Co-authored a research paper that was published to the third IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies (ISGT) Europe Conference; “A Neodymium Permanent Magnet Fault Current Limiter for Use in the FREEDM Project”.

positions.title: Intern
positions.description: Work at Sternco consisted of a high paced environment where flexibility and ease for teamwork were required attributes. Used AutoCAD 2010 to draft preliminary and final designs of mechanical and electrical building floor plans. Completed preliminary building energy consumption analysis for Yuma Alexander Ford. Developed and carried out an air quality test for Yuma Medical Regional Health Center. Organized specs, preliminary and final drawings and overall project files. All my work was supervised by professional mechanical and electrical engineers.

positions.title: Engineering Support
positions.description: At Honeywell I experienced a highly professional work environment were I worked with export controlled information from various countries. I worked for the Global Aftermarket Configuration Management team, Global Business Compliance and Export Control team, and Phoenix Military Repair Development team. All of which required good communication skills, teamwork skills, flexibility to work with multiple teams and consciousness of technology information at a global perspective. The line of work consisted of data management, asset management, and technical support using SAP.

projects.title: SO-ARM101 — Teleoperation & Policy Training (Hugging Face / LeRobot)
projects.description: Brought up a 3D-printed SO-ARM101 arm for teleoperation and AI policy training. Crosses mechanical assembly, embedded/teleop loops, sensing, and ML policy iteration—mech + embedded contact without claiming a production robotics middleware stack.

projects.title: Hardware-in-the-loop testing for Cyber-Physical System
projects.description: Create a communication module with simulink/stateflow to exchange signals between the Renesas controller and CAN communication devices. Using Matlab Code Generation tool to facilitate the development of the module and Renesas API to build the hardware driver.

publications.title: Comparison of Four Different Types of Ferromagnetic Materials for Fault Current Limiter Applications
publications.publisher: IEEE Transactions on Power Delivery · Feb 21, 2013

publications.title: A Neodymium Permanent Magnet Fault Current  Limiter for Use in the FREEDM Project
publications.publisher: IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies (ISGT) Europe Conference · Oct 14, 2012
